/-!
# Erdős Problem 1005

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1005](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1005)
- [Ma42] Mayer, A. E., *A mean value theorem concerning Farey series*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford
  Ser. (1942), 48-57.
- [Er43] Erdős, P., *A note on Farey series*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (1943), 82-85.
- [vD25b] van Doorn, W., *Improved bounds for the Mayer-Erdős phenomenon on similarly ordered Farey
  fractions*. [arXiv:2509.00121](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00121) (2025).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1005

/-- A rational `q` is a Farey fraction of order `n` if it lies in `[0, 1]` and has denominator at
most `n`. (Every `q : ℚ` is stored in lowest terms, so `q.den` and `q.num` are the reduced
denominator and numerator.) -/
def IsFarey (n : ℕ) (q : ℚ) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ q ∧ q ≤ 1 ∧ q.den ≤ n

/-- The number of Farey fractions of order `n` strictly between `x` and `y`. -/
noncomputable def betweenCount (n : ℕ) (x y : ℚ) : ℕ :=
  {q : ℚ | IsFarey n q ∧ x < q ∧ q < y}.ncard

/-- `f n` is the largest integer such that any two Farey fractions of order `n` whose indices
differ by at most `f n` are similarly ordered: it is the minimum, over all pairs `x < y` of Farey
fractions of order `n` with `(x.num - y.num) * (x.den - y.den) < 0`, of the number of Farey
fractions strictly between `x` and `y`. -/
noncomputable def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ x y : ℚ, IsFarey n x ∧ IsFarey n y ∧ x < y ∧
    (x.num - y.num) * ((x.den : ℤ) - y.den) < 0 ∧ betweenCount n x y = k}

/--
Let $\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \ldots$ be the Farey fractions of order $n \geq 4$. Let
$f(n)$ be the largest integer such that if $1 \leq k < l \leq k + f(n)$ then $\frac{a_k}{b_k}$ and
$\frac{a_l}{b_l}$ are similarly ordered, in other words $(a_k - a_l)(b_k - b_l) \geq 0$. Estimate
$f(n)$: in particular, is there a constant $c > 0$ such that $f(n) = (c + o(1)) n$ for all
large $n$?

Mayer [Ma42] proved that $f(n) \to \infty$ and Erdős [Er43] that $f(n) \gg n$. Van Doorn [vD25b]
proved $(1/12 - o(1)) n \le f(n) \le n / 4 + O(1)$ and conjectured that $f(n) = (1/4 + o(1)) n$,
which was proved by Cipollini and GPT-5.5; see `erdos_1005.variants.constant`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1005 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 c) := by
  sorry

/-- The constant in Problem 1005 is $c = 1/4$: $f(n) = (1/4 + o(1)) n$ (Cipollini and GPT-5.5;
formalised by Cipollini, van Doorn and Aristotle). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1005.lean#L44"]
theorem erdos_1005.variants.constant :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 4)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1005

findings.description: The historical sentence on line 65 attributes f(n) → ∞ to [Ma42], but the bibliography defines [Ma42] as Mayer's A mean value theorem concerning Farey series, pp. 48–57. The divergence result belongs to Mayer's other 1942 paper, On neighbours of higher degree in Farey series, pp. 185–192. This is a citation slip; the Lean statements remain mathematically faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Van Doorn, arXiv:2509.00121v1, §1, explicitly distinguishes the two papers: in [1] Mayer proved f(n) ≥ 3 for n ≥ 5, 'which he subsequently improved in [2] to f(n) → ∞'. Bibliography entry [2] is On neighbours of higher degree in Farey series, Q. J. Math. os-13 (1942), 185–192. Erdős's 1943 paper also cites Mayer's theorems on pp. 186–187 in its opening footnote: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1943-01.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Ma42] bibliography entry with Mayer, A. E., On neighbours of higher degree in Farey series, Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. os-13 (1942), 185–192; alternatively add a separate reference and use it for the divergence claim.

reformulations.difference: The source defines f(n), for n ≥ 4, as the largest index separation guaranteeing similarly ordered pairs. Lean instead takes the minimum number of intervening fractions over badly ordered pairs and extends the function to all natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For Farey fractions at indices i < j, betweenCount equals j − i − 1. Thus, if d is the smallest index difference of a badly ordered pair, the largest safe separation is d − 1, exactly the minimum intervening count. Such pairs exist for every n ≥ 4, witnessed by 1/4 and 2/3. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, count_indices and sourceSafe_iff_le_f prove the index-based equivalence. The values at n < 4, including the empty-infimum convention, cannot affect either limit theorem; finite_initial_values_irrelevant proves this invariance.

Tests give f(0)=f(1)=f(2)=f(3)=0 and f(4)=2, and cover orders through 20. The exact pinned external proof and its dependency were compiled together in /workspace/review/full-proof.lean; both the source limit and final linked theorem depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. This corroborates the solved tags, positive answer, constant 1/4, and formal_proof record. The Erdős webpage and Mayer publisher full text remained inaccessible behind Cloudflare; the relevant mathematics and history were checked against the accessible papers above.
